note: Assumptions, imaginary ensembles and exercise inputs for PSY-024, written by hand. Nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository; the observed counts are in observed-input.json.

definitions.share: an actor's events divided by all events
definitions.concentration_index: H = the sum of the squared shares: 1/k for k equal actors, 1 for a single actor
definitions.effective_number: N = 1 / H: the number of equal actors that would give the same H
definitions.half_coverage_count: the smallest number of actors, taken from the largest down, whose shares sum to more than one half
definitions.relative_spread: sqrt(H): the standard deviation of a share-weighted average of independent actors, in units of one actor's standard deviation

hypothesis_thresholds.note: Fixed before analyze.py existed. Part 2 was written down after a first look at the two author counts; the research-cycle record says so.

absent_file_cases.note: Twelve trigger files were deleted without being archived and their content cannot be read from this clone. These cases give them senders by assumption, to bound the index.

synthetic_ensembles.note: Imaginary ensembles of 14 actors, the head count in the department's key principle (PSY-004 quotes it). Event counts are chosen so that every share is an exact fraction.

ensembles.label: 14 actors, the actor of rank r has 1/r of the first one's events
14 actors, each has half the events of the one before
14 actors, one holds 90% and thirteen share the rest equally

aggregate_simulation.note: Synthetic. On each occasion every actor contributes one independent draw, uniform on [0, 1), and the aggregate is the share-weighted average of the contributions. Theory: variance of the aggregate = H x variance of one draw (1/12), mean 1/2.
aggregate_simulation.generator: random.Random(seed + position of the ensemble in the list); draws are taken actor by actor, in the listed order, within each occasion
aggregate_simulation.variance_estimate: mean squared deviation from the known mean 1/2

exercise_2.note: Imaginary log of 100 events from three actors.

exercise_5.note: Imaginary log in which every event carries a persona id. The criterion is fixed before the log is read.

spread_targets.note: How many equal independent actors bring the relative spread of the aggregate down to a target: N = 1 / target^2.

workflow_pushes.note: Assumption behind the lower bound on the workflow's pushes that started no run.
workflow_pushes.assumption: every run that a push started wrote one push trigger, as the workflow file at the pin does; earlier versions of the file were not read, and a run that failed before its commit would break the bound

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical release tracker; it is not Streeling data. The lesson's own exercises use other inputs.
transfer_task.automation_reason: its name ends in [bot] and it writes one event for each release note the others publish

deleted_cases.rule: all deleted events belonged to P
each deleted event came from an account not in the list
